newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus verdict into AIDS trial due July 29.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus verdict into AIDS trial due July 29.

text.p: A Cyprus court will issue a verdict on July 29 into whether a Greek Cypriot knowingly infected his British lover with the HIV virus which causes AIDS.

British divorcee Janette Pink is accusing former lover Pavlos Georgiou, a fisherman, of giving her the killer virus which causes Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome during an affair on the holiday island between 1994 and 1996.

The district court is called to answer whether HIV positive and father of four Georgiou, 40, knowingly or negligently put Pink, 45, at risk and gave her the virus by having unprotected sex with her. It is the first case of its kind to reach court in Cyprus.
Georgiou has denied the charge, filed through the office of the Attorney-General. The charge carries a jail sentence of up to two years, a fine of 1,500 Cyprus pounds ($2,830), or both.
He says Pink knew he was an HIV carrier from the start of their relationship.

"It is our submission that Janette Pink knew Pavlos Georgiou had AIDS...she never understood the implications of it," said Tassos Economou, Georgiou's defence lawyer in his final submission to court on Wednesday.
Georgiou has admitted to having unprotected sex with Pink on one occasion after she took the condom off him when they were both drunk.
But prosecutors contest that the onus lies with Georgiou for leaving Pink open to the risk of infection.

"I can't figure out how a woman informed on the condition of this man -- no matter what their emotional relationship was -- can insist on having a sexual relationship with him," remarked prosecutor Maria Pamballi.
Pink, who came to Cyprus and testified at the beginning of the trial, which started in late May, has accused Georgiou of lying to her about the death of his wife, saying she suffered from leukaemia.
Martha Georgiou was suffering from AIDS, and died in August 1994. Pink has returned to Basildon, in Essex, England, having developed full-blown AIDS. Doctors have given her only a few years to live.
Pavlos Georgiou, whose youngest son is also HIV positive, discovered he was a carrier of the HIV virus in 1992. ($ = 0.529 Cyprus Pounds)
